- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) in recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast baseline or add downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply a “cool-down” decay to forecast after peak.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–), model exhibits mean-reversion bias; smooth forecast curve to avoid overfitting to recent extremes.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture early sharp reversals; add a “lag correction” — delay peak forecast by 1–2 days if sentiment shifts sharply downward.
- If sentiment history shows no strong trend (mostly 0.00), model tends to drift upward; apply a “flat baseline” correction to avoid false momentum.
